text: {"final": {"verdict": "accept", "reason": "The script matches the code and the ticket. load_households(active_only=False) exists with that keyword-only signature and returns all records, so the final save_households(households) persists every record (nothing lost, nothing deleted). same_family in registry/dedup.py matches on Soundex name_key of the head's name plus head.birth_year, exactly as described, and the grouping loop mirrors find_duplicates' approach. is_valid_household_id in core/ids.py validates HH-NNNNC with the mod-11 check digit, so 'kept' is correctly chosen as the record with a valid ID. set_status(h.id, 'merged', merged_into=kept.id) is a real function that accepts status 'merged', sets merged_into, and saves; the redundant in-memory h.status/h.merged_into assignments match what set_status already wrote, so the final save is consistent. The sys.path insert (parent.parent of scripts/merge_duplicates.py) correctly points at the repo root. Groups with no valid ID are skipped with a message rather than merged into an invalid record, which preserves the 'kept record has a valid ID' requirement. No other records or fields are touched."}}
reasoning:
Check the script logic against the code.

1. load_households(active_only=False) — correct signature (keyword-only). ✓
2. Grouping via same_family — matches dedup logic. ✓
3. kept = record with valid ID via is_valid_household_id. ✓
4. set_status(h.id, "merged", merged_into=kept.id) — set_status loads households, sets status and merged_into, saves. Then the script also sets h.status and h.merged_into on the in-memory object — redundant but harmless. Then save_households(households) at the end persists the full list. Since set_status already saved, and the final save writes the full list including all records (loaded with active_only=False), nothing is lost. The in-memory mutation matches what set_status did, so the final save is consistent.

One concern: set_status raises KeyError if household not found — but h comes from the loaded list, so it will be found. Fine.

Another concern: set_status validates status "merged" — allowed. ✓

Potential issue: set_status loads households fresh from disk each call and saves; since the script's in-memory list hasn't been modified before set_status calls (except... actually the script mutates h.status after set_status, but set_status already saved the change to disk). The final save_households(households) writes the in-memory list which includes all records loaded initially plus mutations. Consistent.

Edge: what if kept record's ID is valid but there are multiple valid IDs in a group? next() picks first — fine, ticket says keep the record whose ID is valid.

Edge: what if a group has records where kept is None — skipped with a message; ticket says keep the record whose ID is valid; if none valid, skipping is reasonable, not a bug per se. The ticket says "the kept record has a valid ID" — done when. If a group has no valid ID, skipping leaves duplicates active. But the ticket states duplicates' household IDs are mistyped... hmm, "Some of the duplicate records were typed in before IDs were checked at registration, so their household IDs are mistyped." So the invalid ones are the duplicates to be merged; presumably each group has at least one valid. The script handles the edge gracefully. Not a rejection reason.

Also check: does the script modify other records? No. Does it delete? No.

One subtle thing: set_status saves each time (multiple writes), then final save — atomic via store.write_json presumably. Fine.

sys.path insert: Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent — scripts/merge_duplicates.py parent = scripts, parent.parent = repo root. ✓

Check store.write_json exists — referenced in register.py import; presumably fine.

Everything checks out. Accept.
